text:
adam_acme: Hey team — customer (Acme) on our Dedicated/private stack reports streaming responses cut off after ~28-35s. Client sees partial SSE chunks then a reconnect. Happens only from their corp network, not from home or our hosted tests. Started after they moved to a new Cisco proxy box. Can we triage?

maya_support: Thanks Adam. Do we have a recent request id / example curl to reproduce? Any logs from their onprem ingress?

adam_acme: Request ids: r-9f8b2a3c and r-9f8b2d4f. They used our JS SDK + long-lived token. Repro steps from their side: open stream, get ~2-3 events, stream stops delivering further events, client reconnects automatically and sometimes gets 401 on reconnect.

sam_runtime: Quick checklist: (1) Is ingress tcp_mtu or path MTU causing TCP fragmentation? (2) Are corp proxies dropping idle connections or converting to buffering endpoints? (3) Are keepalives/heartbeats making it through?

linh_sre: I pulled r-9f8b2a3c logs from the Private control plane. On the server side we kept producing events (we see entires in the runtime output at 9:12:10 -> 9:12:50) but the TLS session shows a FIN/ACK to our side around 9:12:34. The client reconnect attempt at 9:12:36 failed with 401 (token validation).

adam_acme: Their network team says the corp proxy enforces an idle timeout of 30s and rewrites Connection headers. They also have deep packet inspection; not much flexibility.

maya_support: Two separate issues then: (A) mid-stream disconnects because proxy kills idles, (B) reconnect failing because token refresh not handled. We need repro from inside corp network or emulate with an nginx proxy that force-closes after 30s.

sam_runtime: Repro steps I ran locally (works to replicate):
```
# simulate corporate proxy that closes idle after 30s
# run a tiny nginx config with proxy_read_timeout 30s and proxy_buffering on
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "http://localhost:8080/stream?model=gpt-test"
```
Observed: server emits comments (our heartbeat `:hb\n\n`) every 15s, but nginx buffers and only flushes when buffer full or after timeout, so upstream client sees nothing then connection closed.
```
# tcpdump to capture server side
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/sse-178.pcap 'tcp port 443'
```

linh_sre: Key finding — many corporate proxies will strip SSE comments (lines starting with `:`) and treat them as non-data, then if no actual non-comment data is flushed, proxy sees idle and tears the connection. Also some proxies convert chunked streaming to buffered responses.

adam_acme: That matches what their proxy team said: they treat comments as keepalive and drop them.

maya_support: Also need to fix the 401 on reconnect: are we issuing short-lived auth tokens that expire between reconnects? If client reconnects after 30s the token might be invalid if TTL is <= 30s. Which token type is the SDK using?

sam_runtime: From logs: reconnect attempt used the same bearer token and was rejected because token had <1s TTL left (our dedicated token TTL was set to 30s for that customer via custom policy). Not good. Two mitigations: extend token TTL on Private/Dedicated for streaming clients or implement short-lived session refresh using refresh token on reconnect. We should default streaming tokens to a longer TTL (e.g., 1hr) or issue a reconnection token parameter that is long-lived.

linh_sre: Immediate engineering mitigation for on-prem ingress config: set nginx (or HAProxy) to these recommended settings for SSE and long polling:
- proxy_http_version 1.1
- proxy_buffering off
- proxy_set_header Connection ""
- proxy_read_timeout 3600s
- proxy_send_timeout 3600s
- chunked_transfer_encoding on
That prevents buffering and keeps idle open. Also ensure TCP keepalive at OS level and shorter intervals (net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=30).

adam_acme: Their infra team says they can't change the corporate proxy. Any workaround on our side?

sam_runtime: A few application-level workarounds we can propose:
- Send periodic non-comment events (a tiny JSON ping) every 10s so proxies see real payload and don't classify as idle. Add a configurable `keepalive_payload` that customers can enable.
- Support a reconnection handshake: client includes `last-event-id` header and we resume from last tokenized offset. But token expiry still a problem.
- Support a short polling fallback for corp networks: if SSE fails, fallback to 5s long-polling to pull deltas.

maya_support: For the customer right now, can we enable payload-keepalive from our side in Dedicated config? Is that a runtime flag per-tenant?

sam_runtime: We have a feature flag `sse.keepalive_payload` we can toggle per-tenant on Dedicated. It will cause the runtime to emit {"type":"keepalive"}\n\n JSON event every 10s rather than comment. I'll enable it for Acme temporarily.

ingress-bot: feature-flag: sse.keepalive_payload enabled for tenant acme-corp by ops (ticket #INC-4321)

adam_acme: After enabling that they confirmed streaming stays alive for >5 minutes. reconnect 401 still happened on some reconnect attempts.

sam_runtime: For the 401s I opened a config change request to increase streaming token TTL for Dedicated Private sessions to 1 hour for customers who enable `sse.keepalive_payload`. Also recommending SDK change: fetch a fresh token before reconnect (if expires < 60s) and/or support a refresh token flow.

linh_sre: Action items:
- ops: monitor r-9f8b2a3c after flag toggle (maya)
- eng-runtime: implement server-side opt-in keepalive payload if proxy strips comments (sam)
- eng-sre: write KB for on-prem ingress tuning (nginx/haproxy) and include tcpdump/wireshark tips (linh)
- devex: update JS SDK to do token prefetch on reconnect (maya + devex)

maya_support: I'll follow up with Acme and share the KB and recommended SDK patch. Anything else?

adam_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. One odd thing: their corporate proxy logs showed many TLS sessions with `RST` after ~28s and sometimes `FIN` with `RST` flags. Could that be path MTU?

sam_runtime: RST after ~28s suggests intentional kill, not MTU. Path MTU issues tend to show fragmentation and retransmits. Still worth asking them to run `tracepath` and `mtu` checks. Also capture `tcpdump -vv` during a hit to see if middlebox is injecting RSTs.

linh_sre: Example tcpdump filters to capture offenders:
```
sudo tcpdump -i any -nn -s0 -w /tmp/acme-sse.pcap 'tcp and host <client_ip> and port 443'
# post-capture: tshark -r /tmp/acme-sse.pcap -q -z conv,tcp
```

maya_support: Closing notes for the thread: we reproduced via nginx buffering, enabling sse.keepalive_payload fixed streaming persistence for Acme. We still require SDK token refresh to avoid 401 on reconnect; assigned to devex to implement prefetch. KB will be posted in sources/slack/support/ — linking once live. :white_check_mark:

adam_acme: Thanks everyone — will loop in Acme to roll out SDK update and ask their proxy folks to allow SSE or at least not strip non-chunked payloads.

maya_support: Marking resolved-for-now, monitoring for regressions. (reaction :thumbsup:)
